name: Old Lavender
lede: Old Lavender is a muted, greyed purple, [[lavender]] with the brightness taken out, and it is a rare color in our painting archive.

sections.title: Lavender, dimmed
sections.body: The library records Old Lavender from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, plate 56 A 7, first recorded in 1924 [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 lists classify it as a purplish black, between [[lavender]] and [[purplish-grey]] [1]. *Old* here works the way it does across this family of names: not an age, but a cue that the hue has been pulled toward grey, the way a worn fabric or a faded [[plum]] might look [1]. The nearest named color in the library is Purplish Grey, about 2.7 units away by CIEDE2000, than to a true [[purple]] [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 46, chroma 12, hue 327 degrees, Munsell 8.3P 4.5/2.5 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in only 49 of 23,781 paintings, 0.21 percent, as photographed [2]. It is most over-represented in the 1910s, in 6 of that decade's 523 paintings, about 5.6 times the expected rate [2]. No single painter here reaches our 3-painting threshold for this color, so no painter stands out as its champion [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [2].
